title: He Left Madrid Thirteen Years Ago. On Thursday, They Called Him Back.
excerpt: José Mourinho returns to Real Madrid on a three-year deal after two trophyless seasons pushed the club into crisis. For Indian football fans, The Special One is back where the drama is loudest.
body:
José Mourinho is going back to the Santiago Bernabéu. Real Madrid announced on Thursday that the Portuguese manager has signed a three-year contract through June 2029, ending weeks of speculation and bringing a familiar, polarising figure back to the club he last coached in 2013.

"José Mourinho will join Real Madrid on July 13, the day preseason begins," the club said in a brief statement.

## A Reunion Born Out of Crisis

The hiring is not nostalgia. It is desperation dressed up as strategy.

Real Madrid have gone two consecutive seasons without a major trophy — a drought that would be unremarkable at most clubs but is existential at the Bernabéu. Xabi Alonso, the man who was supposed to bring tactical sophistication and generational change, was fired midway through the 2025-26 campaign after a string of results that included early Champions League exits and a disintegrating dressing room. Caretaker boss Álvaro Arbeloa steadied the ship but could not stop Barcelona from clinching La Liga with a 2-0 victory in El Clásico — the first time in 94 years the title was decided by a meeting between the two rivals.

Club president Florentino Pérez, who made Mourinho a centrepiece of his re-election campaign, moved quickly once his mandate was renewed. Mourinho left Benfica, where Marco Silva has already been named as his replacement, and flew to Madrid to finalise terms.

## What Mourinho Brings — And What He Does Not

Mourinho's first spell at Madrid, from 2010 to 2013, produced a La Liga title with a record 100 points, a Copa del Rey, and a Spanish Supercup. More importantly, he dragged the club out of six years of Champions League round-of-16 exits, reaching three consecutive semifinals. The team played with an intensity and defensive discipline that had been absent for years.

But Mourinho also left behind scorched earth. His feuds with players — notably Iker Casillas and Sergio Ramos — divided the squad and alienated sections of the fanbase. His infamous eye-poke on Barcelona assistant Tito Vilanova remains one of the ugliest moments in Clásico history.

The 63-year-old returns a different manager. His recent stints at Tottenham and Fenerbahce were underwhelming by his own standards, though he steadied Benfica impressively in his brief time there. He remains one of only seven managers to have won the Champions League with two different clubs. His 26 career trophies speak for themselves.

## Why Indian Football Fans Should Pay Attention

Real Madrid's fanbase in India is among the largest outside Spain. La Liga's broadcast deal with JioHotstar ensures that millions of Indian viewers — and NRIs across the US, UK, and Canada — will watch Mourinho's second act unfold in real time. For a generation of Indian fans who grew up watching Mourinho's Chelsea dominate the Premier League in the mid-2000s, his return to the biggest stage carries genuine emotional weight.

The timing is significant, too. With the FIFA World Cup now under way in North America and the Women's T20 World Cup starting in England, global football is front and centre. Mourinho's appointment adds another major storyline for diaspora sports fans already juggling multiple time zones and tournaments.

For NRIs who follow European football as closely as cricket, this is the biggest managerial appointment since Pep Guardiola arrived at Manchester City. The Bernabéu under Mourinho will not be boring. It never was.

## What Happens Next

Mourinho officially takes charge on July 13, the first day of preseason. Real Madrid are expected to make at least two major signings this summer, with Pérez under pressure to deliver a squad capable of challenging on all fronts. His first competitive match will be the Spanish Supercup in early August. His first Clásico — against the Barcelona team that humiliated Madrid this season — is in October.

"The Special One" has always thrived when he has something to prove. At 63, with the world's most demanding club calling him back, he has never had more.

*Sources: Reuters, CNN, Bleacher Report, NBC Sports*
